subject: Data Engineering
title: The Cost of Bad Data
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Cost of Bad Data.

hook.text: IBM estimated that bad data costs the US economy $3.1 trillion per year. That's not a typo.

buildup.text: Wrong addresses, duplicate records, and stale data waste marketing budgets and frustrate customers.

discovery.text: Poor data quality leads to bad decisions, compliance violations, and lost revenue across every industry.

twist.text: Most companies don't know their data is bad until a high-profile decision blows up because of it.

climax.text: Investing in data quality upfront is always cheaper than fixing the damage bad data causes.

punchline.text: Bad data is expensive. You just don't get the bill upfront.

quiz.question: How much does bad data cost the US economy annually according to IBM?
